authority.abi: No export, signature, #[repr(C)] layout, allocator size/file/line, unsafe lint attribute or detector changed. The repair only narrows the error-path control flow in OSSL_STORE_open_ex.
external_contracts: OSSL_STORE_LOADER_fetch returns one reference the caller owns; OSSL_STORE_LOADER_free releases exactly one caller-owned reference (RC-1/D562; store_meth.rs:225).
ossl_store_close_it releases the context's fetched_loader reference (store_lib.c:592) and the cached_info stack; it never nulls the member.

The method store's cache entry owns its own reference (cache_set up-refs), and the implementation entry owns its own reference (add up-refs); each is released by impl_cache_free / impl_free exactly once.
OSSL_STORE_open_ex: a non-NULL loader_ctx means the loader was opened; every refusal after it must hand the loader to close_it or release the local reference, never both.
A provider set_ctx_params callback may legitimately answer 0; that is a defined refusal, not an ABI violation.

boundaries.mechanism: OSSL_STORE_open_ex error-path ownership of fetched_loader: fetch (one caller reference), transfer into tmpctx, ossl_store_close_it release, and the tail release
boundaries.disposition: SAFETY_DISCHARGED (scope: the fetched_loader error-path release; the rest of the file's M1 boundaries are unchanged)
boundaries.contract: At most one OSSL_STORE_LOADER_fetch reference exists per OSSL_STORE_open_ex call. It is transferred to tmpctx when loader_ctx is non-NULL and released by ossl_store_close_it; the local is not released again. When loader_ctx is NULL, no context took the reference and the local is the single release (every fetch-without-open loop arm already released and nulled it). The success path transfers the reference to ctx.fetched_loader, released by OSSL_STORE_close's close_it.

caller_closure.evidence: The post-fix blob has exactly one release site per acquired reference: the else branch at :948 runs only when loader_ctx is NULL (no context took the reference), and close_it at :938 releases the transferred reference. caller_closure.caller: OSSL_STORE_attach:1642 fetch, :1668/:1680 refused-attach releases, :1699-1710 ctx build
caller_closure.disposition: STOP-CLASS DEFECT (B27-X2, out of this single-repair batch)
caller_closure.evidence: When loader_set_params refuses (:1672) after p_attach answered a live loader_ctx, p_close closes that context and fetched_loader is freed and nulled, but the local loader_ctx stays non-NULL. The function then allocates ctx and publishes loader = NULL, fetched_loader = NULL, loader_ctx = closed pointer. OSSL_STORE_close -> ossl_store_close_it takes the fetched_loader == NULL branch and dereferences (*ctx).loader (NULL) at store_lib.rs:652; OSSL_STORE_load does the same at :1273. The authority has the identical defect (store_lib.c:1093-1098 then :585-590). A C-valid params array refused by the provider (repeated properties key, or expect with a wrong type) reaches it. Not repaired here; recorded as the next boundary repair.

escalations.class: NULL dereference after a provider set_ctx_params refusal
escalations.description: OSSL_STORE_attach's fetched branch assigns loader_ctx before loader_set_params; when loader_set_params refuses, p_close closes the context and fetched_loader is freed and nulled, but loader_ctx remains non-NULL. The ctx is published with loader = NULL and fetched_loader = NULL. OSSL_STORE_close's ossl_store_close_it then executes the fetched_loader == NULL arm and dereferences (*ctx).loader (NULL); OSSL_STORE_load reaches the same member earlier. The authority has the identical defect at store_lib.c:1093-1098 (ctx->loader = fetched_loader = NULL with loader_ctx non-NULL) and :585-590 (ctx->loader->closefn).
escalations.reachability: C-valid: a params array the provider legitimately refuses (for the file row, a repeated properties key makes file_set_ctx_params_decoder answer None, or an expect parameter with the wrong type makes OSSL_PARAM_get_int fail). loader_set_params then answers 0 and the branch runs.
escalations.scope: Out of this single-repair batch by instruction. Proposed repair: clear loader_ctx (and do not publish the context) when the params refusal closes it, or keep the authority's return-NULL intent; control: an attach probe with a refused params array that then calls OSSL_STORE_close and OSSL_STORE_load under ASan.
